It raised a $9.5M seed in January 2026 from Quiet Capital, Slow Ventures, and Moxxie, and is part of Y Combinator's W26 batch, consistently doubling revenue.
investors: Quiet Capital; Slow Ventures; Moxxie Ventures; Y Combinator
notes: No independent website confirmed as of Sep 2026; YC page used as canonical link.

about: Banking and financial stack for startups and SMBs
description: Mercury provides banking, credit cards, and Treasury for startups, scaling to 200K+ customers. It raised a $200M Series D at a $5.2B valuation in May 2026, led by TCV — up 49% in 14 months — as applications jumped 2.5x year-over-year.
investors: TCV; Sequoia Capital; a16z; CRV; Coatue

about: Financial data network connecting apps to 12,000+ banks
description: Plaid operates the leading financial data network powering payments, lending, and fintech apps, connecting to 12,000+ institutions. It secured an $8B valuation in a February 2026 round and employee share sale, up 31% from $6.1B in April 2025, with a long-anticipated IPO reportedly on deck.
investors: Franklin Templeton; Khosla Ventures; Silver Lake; Altos Ventures

about: AI-powered corporate cards, spend management, and procurement
description: Ramp provides corporate cards and AI-driven spend management that automates expense workflows and finds savings. It raised $750M at a $44B valuation on June 4, 2026 — led by ICONIQ, GIC, and Ontario Teachers' — up from $32B in November 2025, after surpassing $1B in annualized revenue.
investors: ICONIQ; GIC; Ontario Teachers' Pension Plan; Founders Fund; Thrive Capital

about: Payments and programmable financial infrastructure for the internet
description: Stripe is the private fintech giant powering internet payments, now near $2T in total volume processed. A February 2026 employee tender offer valued it at $159B — a 70%+ jump — led by Thrive, Coatue, and a16z, and it agreed in August 2026 to acquire AI model gateway OpenRouter for $7.5B as it builds the transaction layer for AI agents.
investors: Thrive Capital; Coatue Management; a16z; Sequoia Capital; GV
status_note: IPO widely anticipated; last primary round $6.5B Series I at $50B (2023).

about: AI clinical documentation and care intelligence from conversations
description: Abridge converts clinician-patient conversations into structured medical notes and revenue-cycle data, deployed at health systems including Epic-integrated UPMC. It raised a $300M Series E at a $5.3B valuation led by a16z in June 2025, reaffirmed by a $316M Series E extension; total funding is ~$773M with ~2,000 employees.
investors: a16z; Khosla Ventures; Lightspeed Venture Partners; Bessemer Venture Partners; Emerson Collective

about: AI sales and customer-service agents for home services
description: Avoca provides AI agents that answer, qualify, and book jobs for HVAC, plumbing, and home-service companies, and was among the fastest-scaling vertical AI startups. It has raised $125M across 3 rounds from Meritech, General Catalyst, Kleiner Perkins, and Y Combinator, with a 2026 round and $1B in booked jobs on track.
investors: Meritech Capital; General Catalyst; Kleiner Perkins; Amplify Partners; Y Combinator
notes: Original repo categorized as HealthTech with SF HQ — corrected (NYC; vertical AI for home services).

about: AI employees for primary care practices (YC W26)
description: Beacon Health builds AI agents that work inside any EHR like a human employee, doubling revenue for primary care practices while reducing total cost of care. It emerged from Y Combinator's W26 batch with ~$5.4M in early funding from YC and primary-care physicians.
investors: Y Combinator; Primary-care physicians & founders

about: Safety-focused AI agents for patient-facing healthcare tasks
description: Hippocratic AI builds voice AI agents for non-diagnostic patient tasks — pre-op prep, follow-ups, medication reminders — with an emphasis on safety certification. It raised a $126M Series C at a $3.5B valuation in November 2025, led by Avenir Growth, after a $141M Series B at $1.64B in January 2025.
investors: Avenir Growth; General Catalyst; Kleiner Perkins; Nvidia; Universal Health Services

about: AI-powered primary care combining data and telehealth
description: K Health provides AI-driven primary care — symptom assessment plus clinician-backed telehealth — using anonymized health records for triage. Its most recent major round was ~$50M in July 2024 led by Claure Group; total funding across 13 rounds is ~$439M.
investors: Claure Group; General Catalyst; Bold Capital; 3L; Mangrove Capital
notes: Original repo listed 'Series E $132M' — corrected per primary reporting.

about: AI medical knowledge platform used by 40% of US physicians
description: OpenEvidence provides an AI-powered evidence search and clinical decision platform that became the fastest-adopted physician tool in history, free for verified clinicians and monetized via pharma advertising. It closed a $250M Series D at a $12B valuation in January 2026, with annualized revenue hitting $300M and reports of a raise at $20B in July 2026.
investors: Sequoia Capital; Kleiner Perkins; Coatue Management; GV; Conviction
source: Becker's Hospital Review, mobihealthnews, PR Newswire
notes: Jul 2026: reportedly weighed $200M raise at $20B (The Information).

about: AI care-coordination and disease-detection platform for hospitals
description: Viz.ai detects strokes and other acute conditions from medical imaging and coordinates care teams in real time across 1,600+ hospitals. Its last priced round was a $100M Series D at a $1.2B valuation in April 2022; total funding is ~$252M across seven rounds.
investors: Tiger Global; Insight Partners; Scale Venture Partners; Susa Ventures

about: Humanoid robots for home and industry (EVE, NEO)
description: 1X Technologies, an OpenAI-backed Norwegian-American robotics company, builds androids for home and industrial use and launched the NEO home humanoid. It raised roughly $650M across rounds in late 2025 and March 2026 at a valuation above $2.9B, including OpenAI-led financing.
investors: OpenAI Startup Fund; EQT Ventures; Tiger Global; Sandwater
notes: Round aggregates per Sacra; official tranche breakdown not fully public.

about: AI defense technology: autonomous aircraft, drones, and command systems
description: Anduril builds AI-powered defense systems including autonomous aircraft, counter-drone systems, and the Lattice command platform. It closed a $5B Series H at a $61B valuation in May 2026, led by Thrive Capital and a16z — doubling in a year — and was reported in July 2026 to be in talks for a round near $100B.
investors: Thrive Capital; a16z; Founders Fund; 8VC; Fidelity
notes: Jul 2026: Reuters reported talks valuing the company at ~$100B.

about: Autonomous vehicle & defense simulation and ADAS tooling
description: Applied Intuition provides simulation, perception testing, and ADAS tooling to automakers and defense programs. It closed a $600M Series F plus tender at a $15B valuation in June 2025, co-led by BlackRock and Kleiner Perkins — nearly double its prior $8B mark — with total funding around $1.2–1.5B.
investors: BlackRock; Kleiner Perkins; Lux Capital; General Catalyst; a16z

about: Apollo humanoid robots for logistics and industry
description: Apptronik, spun out of UT Austin, builds the Apollo humanoid robot targeting warehouse and manufacturing work, with partnerships including Mercedes-Benz and GXO. It announced a $520M Series A-X in February 2026 — with Google participation — at a reported $5B valuation, bringing total Series A financing to $935M+.
investors: Google; Mercedes-Benz; B Capital; Capital Factory; Terex

about: Autonomous trucking (Aurora Driver); NASDAQ-listed
description: Aurora Innovation commercialized self-driving trucking with driverless commercial routes in Texas since 2025 and is listed on NASDAQ (AUR) since its 2021 SPAC merger. It is included here as a public-company reference for autonomous-vehicle tracking; its market cap fluctuates with AUR shares.
investors: Uber; Toyota; Sequoia; T. Rowe Price; Cargo (SPAC)
status_note: Publicly traded on NASDAQ (AUR) since November 2021.

about: Low-cost hypersonic and strike missiles built on automotive methods
description: Castelion, founded by former SpaceX executives, designs affordable hypersonic strike missiles using automotive-style production. It raised a $1B Series C at a $13B valuation in August 2026 — $800M equity plus $250M credit — quadrupling its valuation from ~$3.4B earlier in the year.
investors: Altimeter Capital; Lightspeed Venture Partners; a16z; Founders Fund

about: Humanoid robots (Figure 02/03) for labor deployment
description: Figure AI develops general-purpose humanoid robots and has begun commercial deployments targeting logistics and manufacturing labor. Its Series C exceeded $1B in committed capital at a $39B post-money valuation in September 2025 — making it the most valuable US robotics startup — and it is scaling production via its BotQ facility.
investors: Parkway Venture Capital; Nvidia; Intel Capital; Aligned Capital; Bezos Expeditions
source: Figure AI (official), The Robot Report, Reuters

about: General intelligence for the physical world (robot foundation models)
description: Generalist AI is a frontier research and product company training robot foundation models for real-world labor. It announced $400M in new funding in June 2026 — taking total raised past half a billion — and quietly raised roughly $200M more within two months per Axios in August 2026.
investors: Undisclosed

about: AI-guided precision manufacturing for defense and aerospace
description: Hadrian automates precision parts manufacturing for defense and aerospace primes using AI-guided CNC factories in California and Arizona. It raised a fresh $1.37B round at a $7.87B valuation in August 2026 — a 5x step-up from January 2026 — with a mile-long investor list per TechCrunch.
investors: a16z; Lux Capital; Founders Fund; Singh Capital Partners

about: Europe's leading defense AI: autonomy software and drones
description: Helsing builds AI for defense — autonomy software, EW, and strike drones — for European militaries and Ukraine. It raised a record $1.8B Series E in July 2026 at an $18B valuation, co-led by Dragoneer, the largest defense-tech round in European history; total funding is ~$3.4B.
investors: Dragoneer Investment Group; General Catalyst; Prima Materia; EQT Ventures

about: Autonomous driving AI licensing platform
description: Nuro pivoted from delivery robots to licensing its Level 4 autonomous driving stack to automakers, with partnerships including Lucid and Uber. It closed a $203M Series E at a $6B valuation in August 2025, with Uber, Baillie Gifford, and Nvidia participating; total funding exceeds $2.3B.
investors: Uber; Baillie Gifford; Nvidia; SoftBank Vision Fund; T. Rowe Price

about: General-purpose robot foundation models (π0 family)
description: Physical Intelligence trains generalist foundation models that give robots dexterous manipulation skills across hardware platforms. Its $600M Series B closed in November 2025 at a $5.6B valuation, bringing total funding to ~$1.1B; Bloomberg reported talks in March 2026 for ~$1B more at roughly $11B, not yet confirmed closed.
investors: Bezos Expeditions; Thrive Capital; Lux Capital; OpenAI Startup Fund; Sequoia
notes: Mar 2026: reported talks at ~$11B valuation (Bloomberg); last confirmed round Nov 2025.

about: Autonomous surface vessels and the Port Alpha shipyard
description: Saronic builds autonomous surface vessels for naval operations and is developing Port Alpha, a $3.2B autonomous shipyard in Brownsville, Texas. It closed a $1.75B Series D at a $9.25B valuation on March 31, 2026, led by Kleiner Perkins — more than doubling its $4B mark from early 2025.
investors: Kleiner Perkins; a16z; 8VC; Elad Gil

about: Low-cost modular AI drones for defense missions (YC W26)
description: Seeing Systems, founded by Matthew and Alexander Le Maitre in London, builds low-cost modular drones that fly complex missions with minimal human input for defense customers. It emerged from Y Combinator's W26 batch and raised an early round of roughly $5M with Pioneer Fund participating.
investors: Y Combinator; Pioneer Fund

about: Hivemind AI pilot for autonomous jets and drones
description: Shield AI develops Hivemind, an AI pilot enabling autonomous operation of jets, drones, and loitering munitions without GPS or comms. It announced a $1.5B Series G at a $12.7B post-money valuation plus $500M in fixed-income financing in March 2026 — a 140% valuation jump in one year.
investors: L3Harris; a16z; Riot Ventures; Washington Harbour

about: General-purpose foundation model for robotics (Skild Brain)
description: Skild AI builds a general-purpose 'robot brain' — a foundation model that adapts to any robot form factor and task. SoftBank led its $1.4B Series C in January 2026, tripling its valuation to over $14B in seven months; total funding now exceeds $2B across four rounds.
investors: SoftBank Vision Fund; Lightspeed Venture Partners; Bezos Expeditions; Nvidia; Menlo Ventures

about: Autonomous sidewalk delivery robots at scale
description: Starship Technologies operates the world's largest fleet of autonomous sidewalk delivery robots, founded by Skype co-founders Ahti Heinla and Janus Friis. It raised a $50M Series C in October 2025, bringing total funding to ~$316M as it expands across US, UK, and European campuses and cities.
investors: Dorset Capital; Matrix Partners; MetaPlanet; One Way Ventures

about: Agentic AI security operations platform (SOC agents)
description: 7AI deploys swarms of autonomous AI agents for security operations, automating alert enrichment, investigation, and response for enterprises. It launched with a $36M seed (Feb 2025) and closed a $130M Series A in December 2025 — an unusually large early-stage round reported by WSJ — bringing total funding to $166M.
investors: Greylock Partners; Index Ventures; Redpoint Ventures
notes: Fast Company Most Innovative Companies 2026, #6 in Security.

about: AI-native behavioral email & human risk security
description: Abnormal AI stops socially engineered email attacks and account takeover by modeling human behavior rather than signatures. Its $250M Series D at a $5.1B valuation (Aug 2024) remains the last priced round; the company, formerly Abnormal Security, continues to expand into human-risk management.
investors: Wellington Management; Insight Partners; Menlo Ventures; Greylock

about: AI-powered security awareness training & human risk management
description: Adaptive Security simulates AI-driven attacks (including deepfake phishing) and delivers personalized security training to reduce human risk. It closed an $81M Series B in December 2025 with NVIDIA, Bain Capital Ventures, Capital One Ventures, and Citi Ventures participating, bringing total funding to $146.5M.
investors: NVIDIA; Bain Capital Ventures; Capital One Ventures; Citi Ventures; a16z
notes: Original repo entry claimed '~$9B valuation' — unsupported by sources; removed.

about: Data security posture management — the trust layer for enterprise AI
description: Cyera provides AI-native data security and governance, discovering and protecting sensitive data across cloud, SaaS, and AI systems. It raised $600M at a $12B valuation in June 2026, a late-stage round that tripled its January 2026 $9B mark; total funding exceeds $1.8B.
investors: Accel; Sequoia Capital; Spark Capital; Redpoint; Georgian

about: AI-native defense against social engineering and brand impersonation
description: Doppel detects and takes down phishing, fake domains, and brand impersonation across domains, social media, and marketplaces in real time. It closed a $70M Series C in December 2025 with American Express Ventures joining, led by Google Ventures (GV), following a $35M Series B in June 2025.
investors: GV; Amex Ventures; Bessemer Venture Partners; Dawn Capital
notes: Series C announced Dec 2025; valuation figure unconfirmed.

about: Cloud & AI security platform; acquired by Google for $32B
description: Wiz built the fastest-scaling security platform in history — agentless cloud and AI security across AWS, Azure, and GCP — reaching $700M ARR. Google completed its $32B acquisition on March 11, 2026, its largest deal ever, roughly one year after announcing intent. Wiz operates within Google Cloud as a standalone product.
investors: a16z; Lightspeed Venture Partners; Thrive Capital; Insight Partners; Greenoaks
source: Google Cloud Press, CRN, PR Newswire

about: AI study notes, flashcards & quizzes from any lecture or document
description: Coconote turns lectures, PDFs, and videos into structured notes, flashcards, and quizzes, popular among university students. It is Y Combinator-backed; Tracxn reports no institutional funding round as of August 2026, so funding remains undisclosed/pre-seed.
investors: Y Combinator
notes: Original repo listed it as 'by Quizlet' — incorrect; removed.

about: AI-first language and learning platform; NASDAQ-listed
description: Duolingo is the world's most popular learning app, with 500M+ registered users and AI-generated lessons via its Birdbrain system. Publicly traded on NASDAQ (DUOL) since July 2021 — included as a public-company reference for AI-native consumer education tracking.
investors: CapitalG; Union Square Ventures; Kleiner Perkins; Ashton Kutcher
status_note: Publicly traded on NASDAQ (DUOL) since July 2021.

about: AI assistant platform for teachers and schools
description: MagicSchool provides AI tools for lesson planning, assessment, and differentiated instruction used by millions of educators. It raised a $45M Series B in February 2025 led by Valor Equity Partners with Adobe participating; total funding is ~$65M.
investors: Valor Equity Partners; Adobe Ventures; Rangeley Capital

about: AI corporate learning & knowledge platform; acquired by Workday
description: Sana built an AI-powered corporate learning and knowledge platform with adaptive courses and an AI tutor, raising ~$138M including a $55M round led by NEA. Workday signed a definitive agreement to acquire the company for approximately $1.1B in September 2025 — its largest deal ever — and completed the acquisition shortly after.
investors: NEA; Workday Ventures; Atomica; Heartcore Capital
